an-s-coffee-ta-xua: A wooden balcony in Đỉnh Gió facing straight onto the valley; on cloud-season mornings the clouds sit right below your chair.

An's Coffee is in the Đỉnh Gió area, one of the cloud-hunting ridges closest to central Tà Xùa. The best spot is the **outdoor wooden deck**: a row of wooden chairs right against the railing, looking straight out over the valley and layer upon layer of distant mountains.

In cloud season, around 6–8am the sea of clouds fills the valley right in front of you. On clear days you get the whole green mountain range instead, perfect for a slow cup of coffee.

The café serves food, handy for breakfast after cloud hunting or for staying the whole morning.

**Good for:** anyone wanting a quiet seat, photos on a wooden balcony facing the clouds, or a light breakfast in Đỉnh Gió.
cafe-lang-van-hoa: A gravel yard full of hydrangeas and a porch hung with red lanterns facing the mountains; coffee plus a hot meal.

Cafe Làng Văn Hóa in the Đỉnh Gió area has a **gravel yard planted with hydrangeas**, a porch hung with red lanterns, and mountains and clouds in the distance. When the flowers bloom it is a photo spot full of village atmosphere.

It doesn't just serve drinks but also **rice meals**: familiar home-style dishes such as tofu in tomato sauce and stir-fried pork, eaten with hot steamed rice. In the evening the green-roofed house lights up warmly, and you can sit for a long time without feeling cold.

**Good for:** groups wanting coffee and a proper meal in one place, flower lovers and anyone who likes a village-style setting.
chillout-village-nha-hang-cafe: The restaurant & café of Chillout Village resort in Khe Cải: outdoor pool, glass-walled dining room facing the clouds, evening bonfires.

Chillout Village is a resort in Khe Cải village, and its restaurant and café are open to visitors too. The most striking feature is the **outdoor swimming pool** among rows of earth-walled, tile-roofed houses, with stone paths lined with roses.

The **glass-walled dining room** looks straight out at the mountains; on cloudy days your table seems to float on the sea of clouds. In the evening there's a **bonfire** in the yard, ideal for groups of friends grilling and chatting late into the night.

Khe Cải is quieter than the centre, so this is a convenient place to eat for guests at homestays around the village.

**Good for:** groups and families wanting an unhurried meal, photos of a pool in the mountains, evening bonfires.

See the rooms: [Chillout Village](/homestay/chillout-village).
cloud-coffee-cloud-forest-ta-xua: A warm wooden coffee counter at Cloud Forest, Chung Trinh village, among wooden houses looking straight down into the cloudy valley.

Cloud Coffee is the coffee counter of **Cloud Forest Tà Xùa**, a cluster of wooden houses hidden in the forest in Chung Trinh village. Step through the stone gate with its carved wooden sign and you'll find a **wooden bar lit with warm yellow lights**, perfect for cold, misty mornings.

The whole site looks straight down into the valley and Chung Trinh village. In cloud season the clouds drift right below the wooden houses, so sipping coffee here feels like sitting above the clouds. Resident cats wander around too, much loved by guests.

**Good for:** people who like forest settings, quiet and a retreat feel, or want to see Cloud Forest before booking a room.

See the wooden houses: [Cloud Forest Tà Xùa](/homestay/cloud-forest-ta-xua).
ca-phe-ban-song-lung-khung-long:
Cà phê Bản sits right on the road up to the **Dinosaur Spine (Sống lưng khủng long)**, the most famous and most remote viewpoint in Tà Xùa. After the long ride it's the perfect stop: a roof overhead, roadside parking and hot food.

It opens at **5am**, in time for sunrise hunters. Inside, cloth-curtained windows open onto a long **sea of clouds**; late in the afternoon the sun sets right behind the mountains opposite. It serves light breakfasts such as salad, eggs and sausage to fuel you up before the walk out onto the ridge.

**Good for:** people visiting the Dinosaur Spine who need a rest stop, breakfast, or a place to wait for the clouds or the sunset before heading back.

Read more: [Dinosaur Spine, Tà Xùa](/kinh-nghiem/song-lung-khung-long-ta-xua).
ca-phe-thang-10: A wooden house with a wide porch in central Tà Xùa, a stone-paved yard, red bunting and flowers out front; sit outside as long as you like.

Cà phê Tháng 10 in central Tà Xùa is a **wooden house with a wide porch**, with a stone-paved yard, flower pots and red bunting out front. The space is rustic and bright, a place to linger rather than snap a quick photo.

The best seats are the **tables on the porch**, watching mountain-town life go by. Drinks are the familiar ones like black coffee and hot cocoa, with snacks such as sunflower seeds and dried nibbles, just right for chatting on a cold day.

Being in the centre, it's an easy walk from nearby homestays.

**Good for:** people staying in the centre wanting a chill afternoon seat, or friends catching up without going far.
hien: A yellow-walled bar with patterned tiles and brocade, plus a wide outdoor wooden deck facing the Đỉnh Gió valley.

Hiên ("Porch") is a café in the Đỉnh Gió area and, true to its name, its best feature is a **very wide outdoor wooden deck** stretching out towards the valley. From here the whole range of hills lies before you, and in cloud season the clouds blanket everything below.

Inside, the bar is decorated with **yellow walls, patterned tiles and ethnic brocade**, cosy on cold misty days. It serves food too: a hot bowl and a glass of orange juice by the railing make a very "Tà Xùa" breakfast. Dogs and cats sunbathe around the café, giving it a homely feel.

**Good for:** people who like sitting outside with a wide view, a light breakfast after cloud hunting, photos on the wooden deck.
hien-nha-tren-thao-nguyen: A glass-walled wooden house on the Tà Xùa Grassland facing grassy hills and white tents; warm inside, grass just outside.

Hiên Nhà trên Thảo Nguyên is right on the **Tà Xùa Grassland**, in the same cluster as Dolphin Rock and the Lonely Tree. The café is a **long wooden house with big glass walls** and rustic wooden furniture, with views straight out onto green grassy hills and white tents in the distance.

The nice thing is the choice: on cold, windy days sit inside behind the glass; on sunny days take a chair **out onto the grassy hill** for photos. When the fog rolls in the whole grassland turns misty white, very atmospheric.

**Good for:** people visiting the Grassland – Dolphin Rock – Lonely Tree cluster who need a drink stop and photos on the grass.

Read more: [Dolphin Rock & the Lonely Tree](/kinh-nghiem/mom-ca-heo-cay-co-don-ta-xua).
khe-cai-coffee-ngay-nao-do: A café in Khe Cải with a spot to watch sunrise over the sea of clouds; opens at 6am, right when the clouds are best.

Khe Cải Coffee (also called Ngày Nào Đó) is in Khe Cải village, further from the centre and therefore much quieter. It opens **from 6am**, right in cloud-hunting hours.

Its best feature is the **sunrise viewpoint**: the sun rises behind the mountains while the sea of clouds fills the valley below. Right by the café there's a jutting ledge to stand on for photos over the whole valley. On less cloudy days there are still green mountains, flowers and a hot coffee in a ceramic cup.

**Good for:** people staying in Khe Cải, sunrise lovers who avoid crowds, and anyone wanting a photo standing on a mountain ledge.

Read more: [Cloud-watching cafés in Tà Xùa by area](/kinh-nghiem/quan-ca-phe-san-may-ta-xua-theo-khu).
khen-coffee-house: A café and homestay in the Đỉnh Gió area: flower and vegetable gardens and a raised wooden hut with a flower-covered staircase for photos.

Khèn Coffee House is a café attached to a homestay in the Đỉnh Gió area, with most rooms looking straight onto the sea of clouds. The café is open to visitors and has a **very large garden**: brick paths, flower beds and even the family's green vegetable garden.

Its most famous spot is the **little raised wooden hut with a flower-covered staircase**, sky and clouds behind it, where almost everyone queues for a photo. There are also wooden decks and plenty of seats around the garden.

**Good for:** photo lovers, garden settings, families with young children who need space to run around.

See the rooms: [Khèn Coffee House Tà Xùa](/homestay/khen-coffee-house-ta-xua).
lili-mountain-tiem-ca-phe-tu-te: A small wooden café in Khe Cải with matcha, beautifully layered drinks and tables facing a misty valley.

Lili Mountain – Tiệm cà phê Tử Tế is a **small café with a dark wooden front** in Khe Cải village. It's not noisy, ideal for people who like to sit slowly.

The highlight is the **carefully made drinks**: matcha whisked with a bamboo whisk, cinnamon-dusted lattes, layered blue-and-yellow drinks topped with small flowers. Outdoor tables look down into the valley; when the mist comes in the whole scene behind your glass turns soft white, great for photos.

**Good for:** matcha fans and lovers of pretty drinks, couples, and anyone who likes small quiet cafés away from the centre.
mi-ami-mountain-retreat-cafe-nha-hang: A wooden house glowing warmly in Đỉnh Gió, both café and restaurant, food served on handsome ceramics; rooms with big glass windows too.

Mi Ami Mountain Retreat in the Đỉnh Gió area is a cluster of **wooden houses** combining a café, restaurant and guest rooms. In the evening the main house glows golden, looking very cosy against the cold mountain night.

Food is **served on ceramic bowls and plates** with fresh flowers on the table, suited to an unhurried meal rather than a quick bite. A very friendly long-haired white cat lives here. Besides the dining area there are rooms with **big glass windows facing the mountains**.

**Good for:** couples, cosy dinners, and people who like a wooden-house retreat atmosphere.
moong-homestay-coffee: A homestay and café in Đỉnh Gió: a wooden walkway down the hillside and wooden balconies facing tea hills and distant mountains.

Moong Homestay & Coffee sits on a hillside in the Đỉnh Gió area. From the café a **wooden walkway runs along the rooftops down the slope**, strung with fairy lights that look lovely at night.

The main seats are **wooden balconies jutting out over the valley**, looking down onto green tea hills and distant mountain ridges. On clear days you can see the whole range; on cloud-season mornings the valley turns white. There's also a railing corner with a flag for photos, and a family dog that often sits watching the view with guests.

**Good for:** people who like wide mountain views, wooden balcony photos, or are looking for a small homestay in Đỉnh Gió.
may-bay-coffee: A wooden-roofed café in Đỉnh Gió, hot cocoa with marshmallows and a spot to watch the sun set behind the mountains.

Mây Bay Coffee is in the Đỉnh Gió area, easy to spot by its **wooden porch roof** and carved wooden name sign. It serves food and plenty of hot drinks, including a **hot cocoa with marshmallows** that's perfect on cold days.

Mây Bay's best feature is the **sunset**: the sun goes down right behind the mountains in front, the sky turns orange-red and the green hills below change colour. If you hunted clouds in the morning, coming back here in the afternoon for the sunset rounds off the day.

**Good for:** sunset lovers, groups spending the late afternoon, fans of hot drinks.

Read more: [5 sunset spots in Tà Xùa](/kinh-nghiem/ngam-hoang-hon-ta-xua).
may-ban-ta-xua-homestay-coffee: A homestay & café in Mống Vàng: wooden houses, a lantern-lit wooden gate, a large yard with car parking and a sunset view.

Mây Bản Tà Xùa in the Mống Vàng area is a homestay with a café on site. The entrance has a **large rock carved with its logo**, behind which are rows of wooden houses, flower gardens and a **tile-roofed wooden gate hung with yellow lanterns**.

The yard is large, with **car parking**, convenient for self-drive guests and groups. The view opens onto the valley, lovely for sunsets in the late afternoon; at night the houses light up warmly. The homestay serves food and coffee on site and rents motorbikes.

**Good for:** self-drive guests, large groups, and people staying in Mống Vàng who need somewhere nearby to eat.

See the rooms: [Mây Bản Tà Xùa](/homestay/may-ban-ta-xua).
man-the-cocktail-bar:
MẬN – The Cocktail Bar in central Tà Xùa is a **rare cocktail bar in the mountains**. A long wooden bar with shelves of bottles covering the wall, blue neon lights, paintings and high tables looking out on the mountain town at night.

Evenings here are lively with upbeat music, ideal for groups of friends wanting a change after a day of cloud hunting and barbecue. If you're used to daytime coffee, a cocktail in the cold mountain air is a completely different experience.

**Good for:** young groups of friends, people who enjoy nightlife and want an evening beyond hotpot and barbecue.

*Note: if you've been drinking, don't ride a motorbike back to your homestay, especially on mountain roads at night.*
nha-cua-an-homestay-coffee: A gravel yard with folding chairs under umbrellas facing the valley, wildflowers on the tables, and hot noodle soup for breakfast.

Nhà Của An Homestay & Coffee has a **large gravel yard with canvas folding chairs and umbrellas**, all facing the valley. Simple vases of wildflowers sit on the tables, great for photos.

The café serves **hot breakfasts** such as noodle soup and beef phở with egg, eaten right by the railing overlooking the sea of clouds. Down the grassy slope is a small wooden hut, a favourite photo spot. The café is within the grounds of the 10-room Nhà của An homestay.

**Good for:** breakfast after cloud hunting, chilling outdoors, photos of folding chairs and umbrellas facing the mountains.

See the rooms: [Nhà của An](/homestay/nha-cua-an-ta-xua).
nha-h-mong:
Nhà H'Mông is a wooden-house café in central Tà Xùa, easy to recognise by the **"Nhà H'Mông cà phê" sign** on its wooden roof and the row of wooden chairs on the porch.

What sets it apart is that it **opens from 6:30am to 11pm**. Many places in Tà Xùa close early in the evening, but here you'll still find a warm seat and food, good for people arriving late or groups wanting to stay out after dinner. Early in the morning the fog wraps around the roof, and a hot coffee here feels very much like the mountains.

**Good for:** people staying in the centre who need a late-night seat, a light snack or shelter from the cold.
noong-oi-homestay-coffee: A homestay café in a pine forest in Khe Cải: wooden porches, glass walls for sunset over the clouds, tables built around tree trunks.

Noong Ơi Homestay Coffee is in Khe Cải village, among a **pine forest**, wooden porches and small wooden houses. It feels very much like the forest: wooden tables built around tree trunks, yellow flowers blooming along the paths.

The best spot is the **glass wall facing the sea of clouds at sunset**, with the sky turning pink and orange behind the mountains. If you want to stay, the homestay has small rooms in the forest, including a bathtub corner right by a glass wall facing the mountains.

**Good for:** pine-forest lovers, couples, and anyone wanting a sunset in quiet Khe Cải.

See the rooms: [Noong ơi Homestay](/homestay/noong-oi-homestay).
sunset-clouds-coffee: The café of Sunset Clouds: a wooden pavilion facing the sea of clouds and sunset, and A-frame glass houses glowing at night.

Sunset Clouds Coffee is the café of the **Sunset Clouds Tà Xùa** homestay in Chung Trinh village. True to its name, it's the place to **watch the sunset over the sea of clouds**: the sun sinks behind the mountains while clouds fill the valley below the wooden pavilion.

Morning sunshine over the clouds is just as beautiful. At night the homestay's row of **A-frame glass houses** lights up and the paths are strung with fairy lights, sparkling when seen from above.

**Good for:** sunset hunters, couples, and anyone wanting a preview of the Sunset Clouds homestay.

See the rooms: [Sunset Clouds Tà Xùa](/homestay/sunset-clouds-ta-xua).
tram-may-ta-xua-2: A wooden house with red flags in Khe Cải, a large gravel yard and a railing facing straight onto the sea of clouds; food served.

Trạm Mây Tà Xùa in Khe Cải village is a **wooden house hung with strings of red flags**, with a large gravel yard, flower pots and small tables in front. Behind it is a **railing facing straight onto the sea of clouds**; in cloud season you can stand right there for photos with white clouds stretching to the horizon.

It serves food, so you can eat and watch the clouds in one place. Also in Khe Cải is the Trạm Mây hotpot and barbecue shop for dinner.

**Good for:** people staying in Khe Cải, anyone wanting to watch clouds without big crowds, photos at the cloud-sea railing.
bep-an-xuan-thi-ta-xua:
Bếp ăn Xuân Thì in central Tà Xùa specialises in **home-style set meals**: fried eggs, braised pork, boiled vegetables, soup, tofu, with watermelon for dessert. Prices start **from 90.000đ**, enough to fill you up for lunch on a busy itinerary.

The space is a wooden house decorated with **indigo cloth and brocade**, with a large covered dining area hung with red flags for big groups. In the evening the porch is strung with fairy lights facing the hills, lovely when the sky turns pink.

**Good for:** a quick lunch, families with young children and older relatives wanting familiar rice dishes, budget groups.
com-nha-namiya-dinh-gio:
Cơm nhà Namiya in the Đỉnh Gió area serves **family-style rice meals**: stir-fried pork, stir-fried vegetables, roasted peanuts, pork roll, soup and steamed rice, neatly arranged on wooden trays. Simple but filling, ideal after a morning of cloud hunting.

The restaurant is a green-roofed house under a tree hung with red lanterns, with **outdoor tables** facing the hills. On foggy mornings the whole group sitting around the table with hot rice is very atmospheric.

**Good for:** guests at Đỉnh Gió homestays who don't want to ride back to the centre, groups of friends, families.
mua-quan-ta-xua: A barbecue and specialty restaurant in the centre: generous trays of Northwest dishes, charcoal grills on the table and hotpot for groups.

Mùa Quán in central Tà Xùa stands out for its **very generous trays of Northwest Vietnamese specialties**: grilled meats, sausage, tofu, wild greens, decorated with eye-catching carved carrot flowers.

There's a **charcoal grill right on the table**, and grilling your own food in the cold air is great fun. The menu includes chicken, pork belly, fish, beef and many kinds of hotpot for big groups. The space is warm, suited to dinner after a day out.

**Good for:** groups of friends and large parties wanting barbecue and specialties, cosy dinners on cold days.

Read more: [What to eat in Tà Xùa](/kinh-nghiem/an-gi-o-ta-xua).
nha-hang-a-phu-tinh-hoa-am-thuc-ta-xua:
Nhà Hàng A Phủ in central Tà Xùa is easy to recognise by its **wooden gate hung with red lanterns** and the "A Phu Restaurant" sign. It's a regular stop for many tour groups, serving black chicken, stream fish, smoked buffalo and other Northwest specialties.

A typical table is **hotpot with trays of greens, mushrooms and meat**, plus fries for the kids and a crispy-skinned roast. The restaurant is used to serving large groups, so dishes come out fairly quickly even at busy weekends.

**Good for:** large groups, company trips and families wanting a full spread of specialties. Book ahead at weekends in peak season.

Read more: [What to eat in Tà Xùa](/kinh-nghiem/an-gi-o-ta-xua).
nha-hang-bep-viet:
Nhà Hàng Bếp Việt in central Tà Xùa has a menu of **familiar Vietnamese rice dishes**: set meals with braised pork, vegetables and soup, plus hotpots for groups.

It has an **outdoor seating area looking down over the centre and the valley**; when the mist comes in, clouds swirl right in front of your table. Inside is a large covered dining room with many tables, suitable for whole groups.

**Good for:** families with young children, older relatives, and anyone not used to Northwest food who wants a safe, easy meal.
nha-hang-pho-nui:
Nhà Hàng Phố Núi lies towards **Háng Đồng – the Dinosaur Spine**, where places to eat are very scarce. After walking the ridge, it's a rare chance to refuel.

There's a **large outdoor charcoal grill**. According to the restaurant's menu there are several hotpots (chicken, goat, veal, rice porridge hotpot), specialties such as local pork, mountain goat, local chicken, local duck, salmon and buffalo dipped in fermented rice broth, plus snacks like fries, sweet potato and cheese sticks, and breakfast dishes. Prices are per tray or per whole animal, so ask before ordering.

**Good for:** people visiting the Dinosaur Spine or Háng Đồng who need lunch, groups wanting grilled specialties outdoors.

Read more: [Háng Đồng village](/kinh-nghiem/ban-hang-dong-ta-xua).
nha-hang-doi-may:
Nhà Hàng Đồi Mây in central Tà Xùa has a **wooden balcony facing straight onto the valley**; on cloudy days your table seems to sit on the sea of clouds. A rice meal on a bamboo tray with tofu in sauce, stir-fried meat, greens and steamed rice, with green tea hills behind, is very photogenic.

Besides rice dishes there's hotpot and barbecue for dinner and a well-stocked drinks menu: coffee, latte, yoghurt, juices and tea. You can drop by for a drink in the afternoon and stay on for dinner.

**Good for:** an unhurried dinner after a day of cloud hunting, couples, friends who want to eat with a view.
nha-hang-coffee-gio-ban-ta-xua:
Nhà Hàng – Coffee Gió Bản in central Tà Xùa is both a restaurant and a café, so any time is a good time to drop by. The draw is its **balcony and outdoor yard facing straight onto the valley**, where in season you can watch the **sea of clouds**.

Blue chairs line the railing and the large yard has many wooden tables; on fine days it's busy with visitors taking photos. You can have coffee in the morning, lunch at noon and come back in the afternoon for the clouds.

**Good for:** people staying in the centre who want a cloud view without travelling far, groups wanting food and coffee together.
nha-hang-hang-chu-ta-xua:
Nhà hàng Hang Chú in Khe Cải village is spacious and **takes set-table bookings for groups**. The signature spread is **hotpot with a grill tray** of skewered meat, mushrooms, greens and eggs, plenty for the whole group.

In the evening the restaurant front is strung with fairy lights and easy to find. By day, the **wooden balcony facing rolling green mountains** makes even a hot bowl of noodles a memorable experience.

**Good for:** large groups and friends staying in Khe Cải. Book ahead at weekends.
nha-hang-sammu-ta-xua: A restaurant near the Tà Xùa welcome gate with a large floor-seating dining room on red mats, hotpot and five-colour sticky rice; great for groups.

Nhà hàng Sammu is near the **Tà Xùa welcome gate**, easy to find as soon as you arrive. Its signature space is a **large dining room with floor seating on red mats** and low tables under a wooden roof, big enough for large groups.

Meals include **hotpot, stir-fries, greens and local specialties**, among them the highlanders' **five-colour sticky rice**. Sitting on the floor around a hot pot is a very "village" experience.

**Good for:** large groups, company trips, multi-generation families, and anyone wanting to try floor-mat dining.
tiem-mi-cay-ta-xua:
Tiệm Mì Cay in central Tà Xùa serves **piping-hot spicy noodle pots** with seafood, sausage, greens, mushrooms and egg. On cold days, a steaming pot of spicy noodles is the quickest way to beat hunger.

The shop has a **window seat with curtains facing the mountains**, warm and quiet. Good for evenings when you don't want a whole hotpot, or early mornings right off the night bus when you need something hot.

**Good for:** solo travellers, couples, spicy food fans and anyone wanting a quick meal.
tiem-nuong-canh-cam: A barbecue spot in the centre with long outdoor tables facing the sea of clouds; decorates tables for birthdays and anniversaries.

Tiệm Nướng Cánh Cam in central Tà Xùa has **long outdoor tables right against the railing**, with the sea of clouds and mountains ahead. On clear days, photos here look like you're dining above the clouds.

The main menu is **barbecue** with herbs for wrapping, lime and dipping sauces, plus drinks. The restaurant also **decorates tables for birthdays and anniversaries** with candles, flowers, letter boards and wine glasses, perfect for special occasions in the mountains.

**Good for:** couples, friends celebrating birthdays, a barbecue dinner with a beautiful view.
tiem-lau-nuong-tram-may:
Tiệm lẩu nướng Trạm Mây in Khe Cải village is the place for a cold-evening dinner: **hot hotpot and grill trays** with meat, sausage, greens and mushrooms, plus fried rice and sides. Barbecue and hotpot sets for groups of 2–6 people start **from 200.000đ**.

In the evening, the outdoor seating area is strung with **fairy lights facing the sea of clouds at sunset**; on misty days clouds swirl right around your table.

**Good for:** groups and families staying in Khe Cải wanting a barbecue dinner without riding back to the centre.

Read more: [What to eat in Tà Xùa at night](/kinh-nghiem/bbq-lau-nuong-toi-homestay-ta-xua).
tram-may-ta-xua: A set-menu restaurant in Khe Cải with umbrellas and fairy lights facing the sea of clouds; sets from 249.000đ, best at sunset.

Trạm Mây Tà Xùa in Khe Cải village serves **set menus**, priced **from 249.000đ**. Its biggest strength is the location: an outdoor seating area with **white umbrellas and fairy lights** facing straight onto the valley.

At sunset the sun drops right over the **sea of clouds**, the sky turns orange and the fairy lights come on, a scene that brings many people back. By day there are grassy hills and green mountains stretching out in front.

**Good for:** couples and friends wanting dinner with a sunset over the clouds, people staying in Khe Cải.
vua-lau-nuong-ta-xua:
Vua Lẩu – Nướng Tà Xùa is a large roadside restaurant in the centre with an **easy-to-spot sign**. As the name says, it specialises in **hotpot and barbecue**, with many broth choices, tabletop grills and platters of meat served with greens, cucumber and dipping sauces.

There's an **outdoor seating area facing the mountains**; in the evening clouds drift around while the whole group gathers around the grill.

**Good for:** groups of friends, large parties, a warming dinner on a cold day.
